chapter.title: 比べれば…・～がいちばん

patterns.pattern: ～くらいだ / ～ぐらいだ / ～くらい… / ～ほどだ / ～ほど…
patterns.reading: くらい / ぐらい / ほど
patterns.meaning: To the extent that ~ / so … that ~

formation.form: 普通形 + くらい / ほど
formation.example: 食べたいくらいだ・倒れるかと思うほど

formation.form: 普通形 + くらい / ほど

patterns.connection_notes: な-adj keeps な (×きれいだくらい). Often ～かと思うくらい / ～かと思うほど.
cannot_be_used_for: Exact quantity comparison as a fact
patterns.exam_pinpoint: An exaggerated example illustrating a degree (毎日食べたい・折れそう・倒れるかと思う) → くらい / ほど

confusable_with.difference: That pattern = 'nothing is as ~ as X' (the most).
confusable_with.how_to_choose: Ends in はない/いない → the 'most' pattern.

confusable_with.difference: ばかり = 'only'; くらい = 'to the extent'.

common_traps: ほど cannot be used for 'at least' minimal degree (くらい can: 挨拶くらいしなさい)

examples.japanese: この店{みせ}のパン^はおいしい。毎日{まいにち}食{た}べたいくらいだ。
examples.english: This shop's bread is delicious—so good I'd eat it every day.
examples.note: Example illustrates the degree of おいしい.

examples.japanese: さっき地震{じしん}があった。本{ほん}だなが倒{たお}れるかと思{おも}うほど激{はげ}しく揺{ゆ}れた。
examples.english: There was an earthquake—it shook so hard I thought the bookshelf would fall.

more_examples.japanese: よう子{こ}さんの腕{うで}^は折{お}れそうなくらい細{ほそ}い。
more_examples.english: Yoko's arms are so thin they look like they could break.

more_examples.japanese: 天気予報{てんきよほう}によると、今日{きょう}^は台風{たいふう}ぐらいの風{かぜ}が吹{ふ}くそうだ。
more_examples.english: According to the forecast, there'll be typhoon-level wind today.

more_examples.japanese: かさをさすほどで^はないが、少{すこ}し雨{あめ}が降{ふ}っている。
more_examples.english: It's not enough to need an umbrella, but it's raining a little.

more_examples.japanese: 突然{とつぜん}立{た}っていられないほどの痛{いた}みを背中{せなか}に感{かん}じた。
more_examples.english: Suddenly I felt a pain in my back so bad I couldn't stand.

patterns.book_explanation: 「～と同じ程度だ・～と同じ程度に…。」Used to show the strength of a degree by likening it to some situation.
patterns.one_line_memory_trick: くらい/ほど = 'so much that (picture this)…'

patterns.pattern: ～くらい…はない / ～ぐらい…はない / ～ほど…はない
patterns.reading: くらい…はない / ほど…はない
patterns.meaning: Nothing/no one is as … as ~ (= ~ is the most …)

formation.form: Verb 辞書形 + こと + くらい/ほど
formation.example: 料理を作ることぐらい

formation.form: Noun + くらい / ぐらい / ほど …はない
formation.example: テストほどいやなものはない

patterns.connection_notes: Noun + くらい/ほど + adjective + Noun(人・もの・こと) + はない/いない.
cannot_be_used_for: Objective, verifiable facts (×富士山ほど高い山は日本にない is odd in the exam sense)
patterns.exam_pinpoint: Sentence ends with ～はない / ～はいない and expresses the speaker's feeling 'the most' → くらい/ほど…はない

confusable_with.difference: Same meaning, but くらい…はない is subjective and emphatic.
confusable_with.how_to_choose: Look for はない at the end.

common_traps: Forgetting the ending must be negative (はない)

examples.japanese: リーさんぐらい動物{どうぶつ}好{ず}きな人{ひと}^はいない。
examples.english: No one loves animals as much as Lee.

examples.japanese: ああ、あしたも漢字{かんじ}のテストがある。テストほどいやなもの^はない。
examples.english: Ugh, another kanji test tomorrow. Nothing is as awful as tests.

more_examples.japanese: わたし^は料理{りょうり}を作{つく}ることぐらい楽{たの}しいこと^はないと思{おも}っています。
more_examples.english: I think nothing is as fun as cooking.

more_examples.japanese: 2年前{ねんまえ}に病気{びょうき}だとわかったときほど不安{ふあん}になったこと^はない。
more_examples.english: I've never been as anxious as when I learned I was ill two years ago.

patterns.book_explanation: 「～がいちばん…。」Not an objective fact but the speaker's subjective judgment.
patterns.one_line_memory_trick: X ほど…はない = 'X is No.1 (in my heart)'.

formation.form: 辞書形 + くらいなら
formation.example: 弁当を作るくらいなら

patterns.connection_notes: Verb dictionary form only. Second half: ～方がいい・～でいい・～たい・～かまわない.
cannot_be_used_for: Positive first half that the speaker wants
patterns.exam_pinpoint: First half is something unpleasant; second half says another option is better (～方がいい・～でいい・かまわない) → くらいなら

confusable_with.difference: なら is a neutral condition; くらいなら says the first option is so bad that anything else is better.
confusable_with.how_to_choose: Unwanted option vs. better alternative → くらいなら.

common_traps: Second half that is not a preference/alternative

examples.japanese: 毎朝{まいあさ}自分{じぶん}で弁当{べんとう}を作{つく}るくらいなら、コンビニ弁当{べんとう}でいい。
examples.english: If I have to make lunch myself every morning, I'm fine with convenience-store bento.

examples.japanese: 30分{ぷん}も遅{おく}れて説明会{せつめいかい}に行{い}くくらいなら、参加{さんか}しないほうがいい。
examples.english: Rather than arrive 30 minutes late to the briefing, it's better not to go.

more_examples.japanese: 気{き}が合{あ}わない人{ひと}といっしょに生活{せいかつ}するぐらいなら、このまま独身{どくしん}でいたい。
more_examples.english: Rather than live with someone I don't get along with, I'd stay single.

more_examples.japanese: やせるために好{す}きなケーキをがまんするくらいなら、今{いま}の体型{たいけい}のままでかまわない。
more_examples.english: If losing weight means giving up cake, I'm fine with my current figure.

patterns.book_explanation: 「～というよくない状況に比べれば、…の方が少しはいい。」A subjective judgment of the speaker.
patterns.one_line_memory_trick: くらいなら = 'If THAT's the price, no thanks — I'll take the other.'

formation.form: 辞書形 / ない形 + に限る
formation.example: 映画館で見るに限る・行かないに限る

patterns.connection_notes: Verb 辞書形/ない形 or Noun. Subjective opinion only.
can_be_used_for: Speaker's subjective best choice / best method
patterns.exam_pinpoint: Speaker recommends the best way (やっぱり～は…に限る) → に限る

confusable_with.difference: Different meanings (not only / only in that case).

common_traps: Using に限る for objective statistics

examples.japanese: やっぱり映画{えいが}^は映画館{えいがかん}で見{み}るに限{かぎ}る。
examples.english: After all, movies are best seen in a theater.

examples.japanese: かぜがはやっているとき^は、人{ひと}が多{おお}い所{ところ}に^は行{い}かないに限{かぎ}る。
examples.english: When colds are going around, it's best not to go to crowded places.

more_examples.japanese: 湖{みずうみ}の写真{しゃしん}を撮{と}るならこの場所{ばしょ}に限{かぎ}ります。すてきな写真{しゃしん}が撮{と}れますよ。
more_examples.english: If you're photographing the lake, this spot is the best. You'll get lovely photos.

patterns.book_explanation: 「～がいちばんいい・～がいちばんいい方法だ。」Subjective judgment of the speaker.
patterns.one_line_memory_trick: に限る = 'limited to this — nothing beats it.'
